title: Stephen Biesty's Cross-Sections: Castle
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Slices through a medieval fortress to show the workers, craftsmen, and servants who keep it running, from the drawbridge to the dungeon. Hidden in every scene is a villainous spy to find.

title: Stephen Biesty's Incredible Cross-Sections
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Cutaway drawings open up helicopters, submarines, skyscrapers, and a Spanish galleon, with two big foldouts of an ocean liner and a steam train. Nearly every scene hides a man on the toilet to spot.

title: Stephen Biesty's Incredible Cross-Sections of Everything
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Intricate cutaways follow how everything from a Boeing 777 to doughnuts and newspapers gets made, guided by Chester the Tester and his sidekick Hector the Inspector. Written with humor and plenty of facts, for kids and adults alike.

title: The Story of Buildings: From the Pyramids to the Sydney Opera House and Beyond
author: Patrick Dillon, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: An illustrated history of buildings for young readers, from the Egyptian pyramids to the Pompidou Center, told through the people who built them. Stephen Biesty's cutaways take you inside famous buildings to show how they fit together.

title: Stephen Biesty's Cross-Sections: Man-of-War
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Cuts through an 18th-century warship from the crow's nest to the stinking hold, with sailors at their duties on every page. There's also a spiky-haired stowaway to find on each spread.

title: Stephen Biesty's More Incredible Cross-Sections
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Exploded views of 12 objects, places, and vehicles, from the human body and Venice to a movie studio and a space station. An alien who has lost his way is hidden in every picture.

title: Stephen Biesty's Incredible Body Cross-Sections
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Takes you inside and around the human body, from the brain and bones to the heart, with tiny characters at work in each body system. Two small explorers are hidden in the pictures to find.

title: Stephen Biesty's Incredible Cross-Sections
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Shows what goes on inside 18 of the world's largest buildings and machines, including a castle, a galleon, a coal mine, and a space shuttle. Each illustration is based on real plans, and two of them unfold to a yard wide.

title: Stephen Biesty's Incredible Cross-Sections: The Ancient World
author: Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: Cross-sections and cutaways of Rome, Egypt, and Greece, from the Colosseum and the pyramids to the Acropolis and the oracle at Delphi. Annotations, lists, and explanations bring the ancient world to life.

title: Emergency Vehicles
author: Rod Green, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: A lift-the-flap book with more than forty flaps that opens up an ambulance, a police car, a fire engine, a rescue helicopter, a lifeboat, and more. It shows how each rescue vehicle works on the inside.

title: Into the Unknown: How Great Explorers Found Their Way by Land, Sea, and Air
author: Stewart Ross, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: Unfold spectacular cross-sections to follow fourteen historic journeys of exploration by land, sea, and air. Dramatic storytelling and sidebars explain the key places, concepts, and technology.

title: Rome in Spectacular Cross-Section
author: Andrew Solway, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: Follows a father and his nine-year-old son through a festival day in ancient Rome in 128 AD, from the Temple of Jupiter and the Colosseum to the Baths of Trajan and the Circus Maximus. Every stop is drawn as a detailed cross-section.

title: Egypt in Spectacular Cross-Section
author: Stewart Ross, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: Follows eleven-year-old Dedia and his father on a thirty-day voyage down the Nile in 1230 B.C., during the reign of Ramses the Great. Stops include Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, a mummification, and the palace at Piramesse.

title: Exploring Space: From Galileo to the Mars Rover and Beyond
author: Martin Jenkins, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: The story of how humans made the leap into space, told in Stephen Biesty's cutaway illustrations and Martin Jenkins's friendly writing. It covers life on the International Space Station, the chances of settling Mars, and where we might find alien life.

title: Trains
author: Ian Graham, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: A lift-the-flap book with more than forty flaps that looks inside eight trains, from one of the first steam engines to a high-speed train of the future. Made for a younger audience than Biesty's bigger cross-section books.

title: Giant Vehicles
author: Rod Green, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: A lift-the-flap look inside some of the world's most enormous vehicles, including a double-decker Airbus, the biggest submarine, the largest dump truck, and the biggest helicopter ever to fly.

title: Coolest Cross-Sections Ever
author: Stephen Biesty and Richard Platt
oneLiner: Intricate cross-sections of machinery, industrial processes, and buildings, from a mummy to a rocket. Also includes detailed looks at a medieval castle, an 18th-century British warship, and the human body.

title: Flying Machines
author: Ian Graham, illustrated by Stephen Biesty
oneLiner: A lift-the-flap book with more than forty flaps that explores eight of the most incredible flying machines of all time, from early aviators' aircraft to a luxury flying boat and a rocket space plane. A fact-filled introduction to planes and helicopters.

title: Stephen Biesty's Trains
author: Stephen Biesty and Ian Graham
oneLiner: A lift-the-flap book with over 40 flaps that looks inside well-loved trains from around the world, from one of the first steam trains to a high-speed train of the future. It shows how they work and tells the story of trains.

title: Richard Scarry's What Do People Do All Day?
author: Richard Scarry
oneLiner: A classic Richard Scarry visit to Busytown, where Huckle Cat, Lowly Worm, and everyone else has a job to do, from doctors and dressmakers to grocers and postmasters. Each story shows how a profession helps keep the community running.

title: Mein großes Wimmelbuch
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: The big German look-and-find: a whole life packed on each spread, no words to rush you.

title: Mein Wimmelbuch: Auf dem Lande
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: Ali Mitgutsch's wordless Wimmelbook of country life shows the farm in summer and winter, the vehicles used for different jobs, and a farmhouse museum of old tools. It also shows how farmers lived 100 years ago.

title: Mein Wimmelbuch: Rundherum in meiner Stadt
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: The first Wimmelbook from Ali Mitgutsch, winner of the 1968 German Youth Literature Prize, in which he invented the Wimmelbild perspective. Its busy city scenes are full of small stories told without a word.

title: Mein Wimmelbuch: Unsere große Stadt
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: A bigger city spread; you point at one window, he points at twelve.

title: A Knight's Book
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: Young Wolflieb tells the medieval adventures of his poor but brave master, Sir Frank von Fidelstein.

title: Das Riesenbilderbuch
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: The giant picture book; one page is an evening if you let it be.

title: Rundherum in meiner Stadt
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: A classic Ravensburger Wimmelbook by Ali Mitgutsch with busy city scenes, including a high-rise, road traffic, and a construction site. Kids from age 2 hunt for different motifs on each page, which builds concentration and memory.

title: Mein Wimmelbuch: Hier in den Bergen
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: Ali Mitgutsch's wordless mountain Wimmelbook features daring climbers on a rock face and a crowded scene around a mountain lake. It is full of humorous little stories to discover.

title: Bei uns im Dorf
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: A village day from barn to bakery; the joke is always in the corner.

title: Mein großes Winter-Wimmelbuch
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: Snow, sleds, and crowded windows; he will hunt the same red hat through every page.

title: Mein Wimmelbuch: Komm mit ans Wasser
author: Ali Mitgutsch
oneLiner: Ali Mitgutsch's wordless Wimmelbook of life on and in the water shows fishermen selling their catch, mending nets, and repairing boats in the harbor, plus the inside of a passenger ship and a busy beach.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: On the Farm
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: Six panoramic, nearly wordless farm scenes, from the stable to the rodeo, packed with things to find. Kids meet recurring characters like Jessie the handywoman and unlucky Cousin Grady and tell their stories.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Cars and Things That Go
author: Stefan Lohr
oneLiner: Six panoramic scenes, from a downtown shopping mall to the Wimmeltown speedway, packed with cars, trucks, and things to find. Kids follow characters like Dan the delivery man and Lucky the hungry dog.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Animals Around the World
author: Stefan Lohr
oneLiner: Six panoramic scenes, from the Antarctic to the African plains, with animals to find and stories to tell. A pair of wildlife photographers and a daredevil adventurer are among the characters to follow.

title: My Little Wimmelbook: At the Airport
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: A small board-book Wimmelbook that follows characters on a journey by plane, through check-in, security, boarding, and takeoff. Sized to go along on real trips.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: A Day at the Zoo
author: Carolin Görtler
oneLiner: A day at the zoo in Wimmelzoo, from the wildcat enclosure to the aviary to the monkey house, with hidden characters to spot at each exhibit. Kids make up the stories themselves.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: At the Construction Site
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: Six panoramic scenes, from an underground tunnel to a bustling downtown, with characters like Sarah the architect and Eric the surveyor to find and follow. Packed with construction sights to spot.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Fire Trucks!
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: Hop aboard a fire truck and follow brave firefighters and other first responders from the station to a forest fire to a festival. A seek-and-find scene on every page.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: All Aboard the Train!
author: Stefan Lohr
oneLiner: Follows a busy cast of characters on train rides from Wimmeltown Train Station, from the crowded platform to the aisles of the train cars and the scenery outside the window. Plenty happens along the way.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Good Night
author: Alexandra Helm
oneLiner: Six nighttime scenes, from a slumbering fairytale woodland to a dozing toy store, show hidden characters getting ready for bed. Soothing, subdued colors and activity on every page help kids wind down.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Diggers at Work!
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: A seek-and-find book full of busy diggers and the crew tearing down houses, shoveling dirt, and moving scrap. It includes the series' first spread of labeled diagrams, for spotting parts like the bucket, cab, and engine.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: A Day at School
author: Carolin Görtler
oneLiner: A typical day in the classroom, from drop-off to recess to nap time, with counting and spelling along the way. A cast of kid characters to find and follow is just like the readers themselves.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: First 100 Words
author: Wimmelbooks
oneLiner: Mia and Elias go through everyday adventures, from getting ready in the morning to preschool, shopping, and the playground and zoo. Kids pick up new words everywhere they go in this oversize board book.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Dinosaurs
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: Dino-kids swim, fly, and stampede through the Mesozoic jungle, seaside, and river, from Tyrannosaurus to Triceratops. A seek-and-find scene on every page.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Tractors Everywhere
author: Max Walther
oneLiner: Tractors and their busy workers do a new job each season on the farm, from churning up fields and mowing grass to hauling apples and potatoes. A spread of labeled diagrams helps kids point out parts like the tires, cab, and engine.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: My Busy Day
author: Caryad
oneLiner: One bustling day in Wimmeltown, from a healthy breakfast to school and swinging in the park, with a lively group of kids, families, and workers. Readers see their own daily lives in the scenes.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Find Your Feelings
author: Wimmelbooks
oneLiner: An oversize board book that helps kids recognize and name feelings, from happy and delighted to grumpy and jealous, by reading body language, facial expressions, and context. Kids find characters feeling joy, surprise, or anger in a village, park, treehouse, swimming pool, and magic castle.

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Christmas Village
author: Monika Parciak
oneLiner: It's Christmas Eve in the village, with skating, sledding, shopping, and singing from the outdoor ice rink to the holiday market. Will the little boy get the tractor he wants, and where is Santa?

title: My Big Wimmelbook: Happy Halloween
author: Wimmelbooks
oneLiner: A festive Halloween seek-and-find board book packed with trick-or-treaters, witches on broomsticks, pumpkin carving, costume parties, and a parade of playful ghosts. Kids sharpen their observation skills on every spooky, silly detail.

title: Insect Anatomy: The Curious Lives & Features of Beetles, Butterflies, Ants & More
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: An illustrated guide to beetles, butterflies, ants, and other insects and arachnids. Julia Rothman digs into surprising facts about bees, beetles, and more.

title: Food Anatomy: The Curious Parts & Pieces of Our Edible World
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: An illustrated tour of food from around the world, from a history of eating to global street eats, with a primer on short-order egg lingo and the many ways to serve fried potatoes. Written with food journalist Rachel Wharton.

title: Wildlife Anatomy: The Curious Lives & Features of Wild Animals around the World
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: An illustrated guide to wild animals around the world, from lions and bears to bats, giraffes, and owls. Hundreds of drawings with labels and facts show details down to the anatomy of a lion's claw and a wild horse's hoof.

title: Nature Anatomy: The Curious Parts & Pieces of the Natural World
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: Julia Rothman's guide to the structure, function, and personality of the natural world, from the anatomy of a jellyfish to the inside of a volcano and how sunsets work. Whimsical illustrations come paired with activities that encourage you to look closer.

title: Farm Anatomy: The Curious Parts & Pieces of Country Life
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: An illustrated tour of country life, from the shapes of squash varieties to how a barn is built and what makes up a beehive. Julia Rothman also covers details like crop rotation patterns.

title: Ocean Anatomy: The Curious Parts & Pieces of the World under the Sea
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: An illustrated exploration of the sea, from how the oceans formed and why the water is salty to rogue waves, seafaring vessels, and lighthouses. Also covers sea creatures from crustaceans to cetaceans, and the impact of plastic and warming water.

title: Bird Anatomy: The Curious Lives & Features of Feathered Creatures
author: Julia Rothman
oneLiner: Julia Rothman explores the world of birds, from feathers and feeding to mating rituals and molting, including albatrosses that drink sea water and hummingbirds lighter than a penny. It also covers how birds fly, build nests, and hunt.

title: The Complete Brambly Hedge
author: Jill Barklem
oneLiner: A treasury of all eight classic picture books about the mice of Brambly Hedge, from Spring Story to The Secret Staircase. Through every season, there's always someone ready to lend a helping hand.

title: Castle
author: David Macaulay
oneLiner: A 1978 Caldecott Honor Book that traces the step-by-step planning and construction of a castle and its town. Macaulay's wry humor runs through the drawings.

title: Cathedral
author: David Macaulay
oneLiner: A Caldecott Honor Book that follows the building of the imaginary Cathedral of Chutreaux, with the people of 12th-, 13th-, and 14th-century Europe whose dreams built it. Macaulay's pen-and-ink illustrations made it a classic and a touchstone for budding architects.
A children's educational book about the Egyptian pyramids.

title: The Way Things Work: Newly Revised Edition
author: David Macaulay
oneLiner: David Macaulay's bestseller on how machines work, from windmills to Wi-Fi, explained through the fundamental principles behind them with help from a woolly mammoth. This newly revised edition adds recent technology like touchscreens and 3D printers.
